observation_summary: The DateUtils.truncate method incorrectly handled Daylight Saving Time (DST) transitions because it relied on standard Calendar field manipulation, which can cause unexpected time shifts during truncation. The fix replaces this with manual arithmetic on the underlying time value to ensure the truncated date remains consistent.
reasoning_summary: The fix involves rewriting the internal logic of the truncate method to perform manual time arithmetic instead of relying on the standard Calendar API, which was failing to account for DST correctly. This is a procedural change to the algorithm used for truncation, fitting the 'Algorithm/Method' category.
evidence_used: The fix replaces standard Calendar field manipulation with manual arithmetic on the time value.
The bug report explicitly mentions issues with DST switching hours.
The diff shows the addition of manual truncation logic for milliseconds, seconds, and minutes.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix adds conditional checks (e.g., 'if (!round || millisecs < 500)'), these are part of the new algorithmic strategy to perform manual truncation, not just guards for existing logic.
The fix is a local procedural correction within the existing DateUtils class, not a design-level capability change.
